review:
The most recent update of voice messages is exactly what I've been waiting for! Voice messages have become such an important way to communicate over whatsapp now and the new update allows me to write notes or work in something else simultaneously while listening to my voice notes. Thank you. Plus, I can close my screen and still listen - saving battery life. 

The only other thing at this point I'd love to see are more quality options for sharing large videos or images. Ie: be able to send your content in either a high quality version or dramatically smaller and compressed version (to save data). With that, could you also display how long a video can be to be sent completely, as I've had situations of videos I've made being cut in half due to (I'm assuming) length or size. 

Thank you for constantly making this app even better!

WhatsApp has been around for a while now, it mature, stable and reliable.

However I keep running into this issue whereby voice notes don't play from the loudspeaker, making them inaudible. I’m forced to force close the app and then reopen it, then only will the voicenote play from my phone loudspeakers. I had this issue on my 11, 12 Pro and now 15 Pro Max.

Please fix this bug cause it's seriously inconveniencing to have to force close the app just so that I can hear a voice note. The app must be able to differentiate voicenotes from calls, cause when I experience that issue, my voicenotes will be playing from the earpiece speaker at the top🤷🏾‍♂️...after restarting the app then it begins to play from my bottom speakers

I’m going to try to keep this short (hope this helps).

Honestly… WhatsApp has been improving. From the text messages and addition of features such as : 
- sending video notes, 
-voice notes, 
- and even being able to like statuses
- muting annoying chats, 
- selecting favorite chats 
-mentioning friends in posts 
-channels(the meme and soccer ones especially)
- and finally my bestie meta AI… etc 

 Some say it’s starting to look like Instagram… but honestly it’s a nice app. I actually believe everyone with a smartphone has it (monopoly?). 

 It’s effective and enjoyable - fits right in this world of tech. 

If you want a chill communication app that everyone has (I think should have), WhatsApp  should be in my opinion your first pick. 
 
I'm sure the team’s always working on improving but As a user some suggestions I have that are according to my individual desires/thoughts: 

- giving us options to make it aesthetic with our style while still keeping the WhatsApp feel(fonts, color, layout etc) 
- and maybe allowing us to put GIFs as our profile photos? (just a weird idea) 

We really appreciate all the teams hard work.

Recently my WhatsApp expired.   What a nightmare for the aged.  I am in touch with people suffering cancer and sometimes emotional problems after losing a loved one, whatever.  I didn’t expect that to happen!  What a stressful time I had,  not being able to communicate! Trying to reconnect was such a battle! I was disappointed that when I changed cell phones from iPhone 5s to 7 I lost all my Whatsapp histories. I had thought Whatsapp had its own saving method. I hadn’t saved Whatsapp to the iCloud. I didn’t think that was necessary. Anyhow I found that kind of disappointing. 

I wanted to send Whatsapp’s to myself e.g. when I need to make a quick note about something. I couldn’t do that on my new phone. I had to create a group Whatsapp and delete everyone else but me. Then only could I send Whatsapp’s to myself. 

I get a lot of joy out of Whatsapp. I like knowing that a message is delivered or read. I use voice note to help me memorize stuff. We use video calls to be in touch with loved ones.

I dislike the new version of WhatsApp. My
Phone automatically updated itself and I hate the new version so much. I hate that you now can’t view your own status updates as a list and be able to delete them simultaneously. Now when you click on your status updates it automatically starts playing them all and if you want to delete them, you have to do it one by one. It’s so annoying. Also you can’t hold or pause statuses anymore. They just play even if you want to read something the video or text just passes. I don’t understand why this change was made. It’s a stupid change.

I do not like the new update that has been added to the new community feature where the communities are now added to the main chats column and you can’t access groups individually without having to go through the community. There’s a community tab for that reason. This is tedious because if you are only part of 1 group in the community, you have to go through such a lengthy process to access just that 1 group. And you can’t even leave the community because then you will leave the group you want access to which is annoying. The way the community feature was set before the update was so much better. So changing it back or giving people the option of leaving the community but still choosing which groups they would like to be part of would result in a much better user experience.

Hi there It would be great if you could add an additional feature where you can pre-schedule the sending of a message. There are times when I’m laying in bed late at checking my messages and want to respond, but choose not to, because it would be impolite to send a message in the middle of the night. My overall experience using Whatsapp has been very good. It’s a well-made app with impressive features and it does what it’s supposed to do. 
However, there are some adjustments and improvements that could greatly enhance overall experience. Things that need work include:
1.) Large file sharing - larger media documents are automatically downsized by decreasing the quality. There should be an option you can choose to send the document in its original size.
2.) Dark-mode Compatibility - Whatsapp should be able to be viewed with a “dark-mode” interface based on user preference. It is much more comfortable for some people and would be great feature to help boost the overall ease-of-use of the app.

During the first few years of having my iPhone I never really had many issues using WhatsApp. In the past year or more this app has made my blood boil. Some will say that maybe it’s because my phone is from 2020, it’s getting old. Then why would I still get all my notifications and messages from iMessage the second they are sent to me?! Even when someone calls me on WhatsApp, there’s a chance it doesn’t ring at all!!! 

While typing the volume of the keys just ramps up for no reason, when someone messages me; even when my data is on, it doesn’t notify me or doesn’t even come through for that matter. I have missed important calls and messages because of this app’s incompetence. And just this morning I had missed 2 calls and a few messages that were important to me.

When posting a video on WhatsApp status, it’s frustrating to manually split the video into 30-second parts. Often, I lose track of where the next part should start, which leads to repeated segments or missed content. It would be great if WhatsApp could introduce an automatic video-splitting feature.

An automatic video-splitting tool would streamline the process, ensuring seamless transitions between parts without any overlaps. It could also allow users to specify the end point of the video, making it easier to adjust without the hassle of managing each segment. This would make posting longer videos much more efficient and improve the overall user experience.

This app has been a standout choice for seamless communication over the years, offering a user-friendly and efficient platform. However, recent updates have steered the app towards integrating social media elements, such as reactions, statuses, and channels, which seem to divert from its core purpose as an instant messaging service. While innovation is vital, the addition of these features appears unnecessary for the app’s primary function of facilitating communication. It’s important for the development team to consider allocating their resources more judiciously, focusing on enhancements that reinforce the app’s foundational communication capabilities rather than expanding into areas that don’t enhance user experience. WhatsApp has already established itself as a leading communication tool; maintaining its simplicity and reliability should be paramount.

WhatsApp is an all-round great cross-platform messaging app. I do - however- have one grievance with replying from notifications on the the home/lock screen. Each time I reply (to groups, personal chats, etc) I get a message from WhatsApp saying “⚠️ Could not send reply to ... ⚠️” and when I go into WhatsApp to check, it has been sent. At first this was tolerable but now has become tedious and irritating.

Furthermore, WhatsApp could maybe start looking into message animations like those iMessage use. It makes chats fun and expressive.

Love the app and the way it connects you with people in your life.

The new update make the app busy, if it’s possible, it would be nice to have a way of controlling the app to not have the channels, right now if feels like on your face.  I understand it had to be introduced, but having an option to eliminate it, or deactivate it would be great.

As a long-time user of WhatsApp, I have always appreciated the simplicity of the platform. However, this recent change feels like a step in the wrong direction.

The green color scheme not only feels  unappealing but also lacks the aesthetic appeal that made WhatsApp so popular among users. The previous color scheme was neutral and easy on the eyes, making it ideal for prolonged use. The sudden switch to green feels like a departure from the minimalist design that many of us have come to appreciate. The  lack of options to customise or revert to the previous color scheme is even more disappointing. 

By forcing this new color scheme without offering any alternatives, WhatsApp has effectively taken away that freedom of choice.

Thanks for absolutely nothing!

WhatsApp has always been a reliable way to connect with friends and family and over the last few months, we have seen some updates that really encompass all we need in a messaging app.

Let’s wait and see. 

4 stars for now but an admittedly top performing application. Well done WhatsApp Team.
